summary: This bill amends the National Labor Relations Act and Railway Labor Act to eliminate all provisions allowing contracts that require employees to join a union or pay dues or fees as a condition of employment.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations of any kind.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services.
The legislation has no connection to firearms regulation or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill pertains to immigration, visas, border policy, or related enforcement.
The bill does not address reproductive rights or abortion access.
No references to military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
The bill contains no environmental, energy, or climate-related provisions.
No provisions affect welfare programs, food assistance, or other safety-net entitlements.
The legislation does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
No content related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The bill makes no changes to sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill does not address deficits, debt ceiling, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation contains no foreign aid or international assistance provisions.
Nothing in the bill affects voting rights, election administration, or campaign finance.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or internet policy.

The bill directly amends the National Labor Relations Act and Railway Labor Act to eliminate union security agreements (compulsory union membership or dues). This removes a key mechanism of union power and strengthens the right of employees to refrain from union activity, which aligns strongly with limiting union authority and increasing employer flexibility.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or anti-discrimination law.
